knowledge_point.title: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With the Tangent Trigonometric Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x.$ Applying the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(3 x - 2 \tan x\right) \\ &= -2\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\tan x\right) + 3\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(x\right) \\ &= 3 - 2 \sec^{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y'(\frac{\pi}{4})&=3 - 2 \sec^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ &= -1 \\ &= -1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope is $-1.$
